title: 1 Chronicles 26:20–32
context: Levites placed over the treasuries of God’s house and the treasuries of dedicated gifts, including plunder dedicated by David, Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab, followed by Levitical officers and judges serving on both sides of the Jordan.

verses.text: Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
verses.arminianNotes: Ahijah is over the treasures of God’s house and the dedicated things. Arminian readers see stewardship of offerings as a trust given to faithful Levites.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s resources guarded by appointed servants. The careful oversight of dedicated gifts reflects reverence for what had been given to God.

verses.text: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
verses.arminianNotes: The sons of Ladan the Gershonite are listed, with Jehieli at the head. Arminian readers see family lines entrusted with continuing responsibilities in God’s house.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the genealogy establishing the treasurers’ standing. The precise relationships in this verse are compressed, and readers in this tradition do not press them.

verses.text: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of the LORD’s house.
verses.arminianNotes: Jehieli’s sons Zetham and Joel are over the treasures of the LORD’s house. Arminian readers see brothers sharing an important trust in temple service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see continuity in the care of God’s treasures. The record shows that stewardship was passed on within families of proven faithfulness.

verses.text: Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
verses.arminianNotes: The Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites are introduced. Arminian readers see the Kohathite families taking their place in the ordering of temple responsibilities.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the list moving through Levitical clans in order. The verse functions as a heading for the officials described in the following verses.

verses.text: Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries.
verses.arminianNotes: “Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries.” Arminian readers see Moses’ descendants honored with a place of trust.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the link to Moses through his son Gershom. Readers in this tradition note that “son” in genealogies can mean descendant, so the exact generational span is uncertain.

verses.text: His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.
verses.arminianNotes: Shebuel’s relatives through Eliezer are named, ending with Shelomoth. Arminian readers see another branch of Moses’ family serving faithfully in God’s house.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the line of Eliezer recorded. The genealogy prepares for Shelomoth’s role over the dedicated treasures in the next verse.

verses.text: This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated.
verses.arminianNotes: Shelomoth and his brothers oversee the treasuries of things dedicated by David, family heads, and army captains. Arminian readers see leaders giving generously to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see gifts dedicated by many leaders entrusted to careful stewards. The verse shows broad participation in supporting God’s house.

verses.text: They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair the LORD’s house.
verses.arminianNotes: “They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair the LORD’s house.” Arminian readers see victories acknowledged by returning part of the gain to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see war plunder devoted to God’s house as an act of thanksgiving. Readers in this tradition treat the verse as describing practice rather than prescribing it for every age.

verses.text: All that Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth and of his brothers.
verses.arminianNotes: Everything dedicated by Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab was under Shelomoth’s hand. Arminian readers see gifts from leaders of different eras gathered for God’s house.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see a long history of dedication preserved. The list joins figures with complex records, showing that their gifts were received and guarded.

verses.text: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.
verses.arminianNotes: Chenaniah and his sons of the Izharites are appointed to “the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.” Arminian readers see Levites serving beyond the sanctuary.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Levitical service extending into civil administration. Readers in this tradition note the blending of religious and civic responsibilities in Israel.

verses.text: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of the LORD and for the service of the king.
verses.arminianNotes: Hashabiah and 1,700 Hebronites oversee Israel west of the Jordan “for all the business of the LORD and for the service of the king.” Arminian readers see faithful service to God and king together.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see duties to God and to the king joined. The phrase shows that civil administration was understood as part of serving the LORD in Israel.

verses.text: Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ households. They were sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.
verses.arminianNotes: Jerijah is chief of the Hebronites; in David’s fortieth year, “mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.” Arminian readers see capable people sought out for service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the record noting the timing in David’s final year. Readers in this tradition hold the precise location of Jazer with some caution.

verses.text: His relatives, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom King David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.
verses.arminianNotes: Jerijah’s 2,700 relatives oversee the Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh “for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.” Arminian readers see the eastern tribes cared for.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the eastern tribes included in David’s administration. The chapter closes by showing the reach of Levitical service across the whole nation.
